title: Broken Access Control
text: Enforcement of authorization policy fails, letting users act outside their intended permissions. Can expose, modify, or destroy data, or let a user perform an action outside their limits. As of the 2025 edition this category also absorbs server-side request forgery (SSRF) patterns previously listed separately.

title: Security Misconfiguration
text: A system, application, or cloud service is set up incorrectly from a security standpoint -- default accounts left enabled, unnecessary services running, missing security headers, or overly permissive cloud storage -- creating an avoidable weakness. Jumped from #5 in 2021 to #2 in 2025.

title: Software Supply Chain Failures
text: New in 2025. Breakdowns or compromises in the process of building, distributing, or updating software, most often introduced through vulnerable or maliciously tampered third-party code, build tools, or dependencies rather than the organization's own code.

title: Cryptographic Failures
text: Missing or weak cryptography, deprecated algorithms, or exposed and hard-coded keys leave sensitive data readable in transit or at rest. Was #2 in 2021, now #4.

title: Injection
text: Untrusted input is inserted into a command, query, or interpreter (SQL, OS shell, LDAP, etc.) and executed as though it were trusted code or a trusted query. Includes cross-site scripting as a subtype. Fell from #3 in 2021 to #5 in 2025.

title: Insecure Design
text: Missing or ineffective security controls at the architecture and threat-modeling stage, rather than a single implementation bug -- a well-implemented but poorly designed control still fails.

title: Authentication Failures
text: Weaknesses in verifying user identity -- weak or reused passwords, missing multi-factor authentication, session-management flaws, or poor credential-recovery flows -- let an attacker impersonate a legitimate user or take over a session.

title: Software or Data Integrity Failures
text: Code or infrastructure that doesn't verify the integrity of software updates, critical data, or CI/CD pipelines, allowing untrusted or tampered content to be treated as trusted -- a common vector for supply-chain compromise.

title: Logging & Alerting Failures
text: Insufficient logging, monitoring, and -- critically -- alerting means attacks and breaches go undetected or unactioned even when the evidence exists. Renamed from 'Logging and Monitoring Failures' in 2021 to emphasize that logging without alerting has little security value.

title: Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
text: New in 2025. Systems fail to properly prevent, detect, or respond to unusual or unpredictable conditions -- errors, timeouts, resource exhaustion -- leading to crashes, fail-open logic that bypasses access controls, or leakage of sensitive data such as stack traces.
